paper_metadata.title: Mechanical Properties of High-Temperature Alloy ZhS32 at 1150 – 1250°C

evidence.quote: Castable refractory alloy ZhS32 belongs to the class of precipitation-hardening high-temperature carbon-bearing alloys based on nickel.
Note. The base is Ni.

carbides due to the presence of 0.15 wt.% C in the alloy
The mechanical properties of single crystals of one of the most refractory alloys ZhS32 chosen for the study have been determined at temperatures lower than 1150°C [1].
Specimens with single-crystal structure and specified crystallographic orientation [001] were cast by the method of directed crystallization with seeding agents.
Tests for long-term and tensile strength were conducted for specimens in the cast state (without heat treatment).

Specimens with single-crystal structure and specified crystallographic orientation [001] were cast by the method of directed crystallization with seeding agents. Each specimen was subjected to x-raying to control the crystallographic orientation. The admissible deviation of the growth structure from crystallographic direction [001] did not exceed 10°.
